finding: New task creation is seeded through create_task_with_ledger plus upsert_field_versions, so task rows start with field/event history rather than naked final state.

Universal write enforcement is still incomplete: bin/task done updates tasks directly with raw SQL and no field/event enrichment; bridge_server also retains mirrored raw-SQL task updates even though it compensates with field versions.
task_field_versions.source_event_id is populated from the memory_events line created by upsert_field_versions, so field rows and event ledger stay on the same mutation chain.
Remote status authority is resolved from field timestamps plus event heads before merge, so stale tasks.status no longer wins by itself.
Status normalization happens before merge decisions: remote status is canonicalized and _field_ts is rewritten before field comparison proceeds.
Merge ordering no longer treats local per-machine counters as global truth; packed HLC ordering is preferred before timestamp fallback.
Divergent winner/loser branches are journaled into memory_conflicts instead of disappearing silently during field merge and content-guard decisions.
Per-task export emits _field_ts and conditionally emits _attachments, _links and _tombstone so task files remain self-describing for recovery.
Bridge import hydrates supporting payloads first via import_remote_bridge_data and then enriches task rows from per-task files before merge_import_tasks runs.
Disaster-recovery loading does not rely only on shared.json: load_remote_tasks_for_merge reads index.json and then per-task files for description, notes, links and attachments.
Fresh bridge bootstrap preserves archived/cancelled history instead of only materializing active tasks.
Attachment metadata and bytes now roundtrip together through bridge payloads and attachment file copy logic.
bridge_change_summary counts task, entity, relation, knowledge, provenance and audit churn, so incremental skip-checks see real bridge-relevant movement.
Shrink safety no longer just blocks; bridge sync now auto-heals local description/notes from bridge content before deciding whether to stop the push.
The physical SQLite file remains a hard SPOF for disk loss, external sync interference or human deletion; WAL and event history do not create a replica.
Bridge git repo plus auth is still the single cross-machine propagation corridor: local truth survives, shared continuity does not.
Peer-machine hook/runtime rollout still needs operational discipline and smoke verification; repo fixes do not magically upgrade stale deployed copies.
Bridge-only fresh-machine recovery drill should be rerun periodically on a clean host, not just inferred from code and past spot checks.
